simple.meaning: רֳאִי (rŏʼîy) is a Hebrew action word meaning “sight , whether abstractly ( vision ) or concretely (a spectacle ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Genesis, 1 Samuel, Job, Nahum, beginning at Genesis 16:13. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֳאִי (H7210) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רֳאִי (rŏʼîy) / H7210 is traced through Genesis 16:13, 1 Samuel 16:12, Job 7:8, Job 33:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: sight , whether abstractly ( vision ) or concretely (a spectacle )
definitions.full: H7210. roi רֳאִי noun [masculine] looking, seeing, sight ; — 1 seeing , ר ׳אֵל Gen 16:13 a a God of seeing ( =who sees). 2 appearance ( = מַרְאֶה ), רֹ֑אִי טוֺב 1Sam 16:12 ; מֵרֹ֑אִי Job 33:21 without (healthy, fair) appearance. 3 sight , (warning-) spectacle , כְּרֹ֑אִי Nahum 3:6 . — ׳ר Gen 16:13 b Job 7:8 is Qal Participle suffix

occurrences.englishText: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”
The eye of him who sees me will see me no more.
His flesh is so consumed away that it can’t be seen.
I will throw abominable filth on you, and make you vile, and will set you a spectacle.
